problems.reason: Both sentences state that the first two sacral vertebrae have deep hollow cavities that would have accommodated air sacs in life.
Sentence 3 repeats the meaning of the species name "cluniculus" twice within the same sentence.
Sentence 4 repeats the history of the name Ornithodesmus being assigned to a sacrum thought to be from a bird, then a pterosaur, then a theropod.
Sentence 5 repeats the fact that Harry Govier Seeley first described Ornithodesmus cluniculus in 1887 based on six fused sacral vertebrae.
Sentences 13 and 14 describe the local flora and wildfires of the Wessex Formation, which are about the environment rather than the animal itself.
